mcq.q: What does the join() method do in thread management?

options.B: Pauses the current thread until the target thread finishes

mcq.answer_text: Pauses the current thread until the target thread finishes

mcq.q: Which of the following statements about daemon threads is true ?

options.A: Daemon threads prevent the JVM from shutting down
options.B: Daemon threads must be started with run()
options.C: JVM exits when all non-daemon threads finish, regardless of daemon threads
options.D: Daemon threads have higher priority than user threads

mcq.answer_text: JVM exits when all non-daemon threads finish, regardless of daemon threads

mcq.q: What happens when you call setDaemon(true) on a thread after it has been started?

options.D: The thread is ignored by the scheduler

mcq.q: Which of these is true about setting thread priorities?

options.A: Priorities can be any number from 1 to 100
options.D: Thread priority ranges from Thread.MIN_PRIORITY (1) to Thread.MAX_PRIORITY (10)

mcq.answer_text: Thread priority ranges from Thread.MIN_PRIORITY (1) to Thread.MAX_PRIORITY (10)

sq.q: What is the output when the main thread calls join() on a child thread?
answer: The main thread pauses and waits until the child thread completes its execution. Only then does the main thread resume

sq.q: How can thread priority affect execution?
answer: Higher-priority threads are more likely to be chosen by the scheduler. However, thread priority does not guarantee execution order; it's only a hint. Behavior is platform-dependent.

lq.q: Design a thread model for the above scenario. Implement: Daemon thread for logging Daemon thread for logging Use of join() to synchronize shutdown Use of join() to synchronize shutdown Thread priorities for urgent requests Thread priorities for urgent requests Use of sleep() or yield() for load management Use of sleep() or yield() for load management Provide Java code to demonstrate this design.
answer: class MonitorDaemon extends Thread { public MonitorDaemon() { setDaemon(true); }
public void run() { while (true) { System.out.println("Monitoring memory..."); try { Thread.sleep(2000); } catch (InterruptedException e) {} } } }
class UserRequest extends Thread { private String requestName;
public UserRequest(String name, int priority) { this.requestName = name; setPriority(priority); }

public void run() { System.out.println("Processing request: " + requestName); for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) { System.out.println(requestName + " step " + i); Thread.yield(); // Allow other threads to proceed } } }
public class Server { public static void main(String[] args) throws InterruptedException { MonitorDaemon md = new MonitorDaemon(); md.start();
UserRequest u1 = new UserRequest("Request1", Thread.MIN_PRIORITY); UserRequest u2 = new UserRequest("UrgentRequest", Thread.MAX_PRIORITY);
u1.join(); // Wait for both threads to complete u2.join();
System.out.println("All requests processed. Server shutting down."); } }
